documents.unit: Academic Senate Student Affairs Committee / District
documents.title: AR 5500.1 Standards of Academic Conduct (2024-25 version)
documents.summary: A marked-up draft of the academic conduct regulation. AI appears only as a listed form of academic dishonesty: breaking the AI policy an instructor states in the syllabus or course materials. The rest is general integrity procedure.
documents.stance_why: The document sets no AI rule of its own; its only AI text lists 'Violating the instructor’s AI policy as stated on their class syllabus' as dishonesty, so the decision about AI use is handed to each instructor.

units.why: The regulation lists violating an instructor's AI policy among defined acts of dishonesty ('Violating the instructor’s AI policy'), so unauthorized AI use per the syllabus is classed as academic dishonesty. P36 fits since it is classification as misconduct; P04 is coded separately for who decides.
units.anchor: Violating the instructor’s AI policy as stated on their class syllabus

units.why: The same passage makes the instructor's own AI policy, stated in syllabus, Canvas page or assignment or exam instructions, the standard students are held to; it sets no university stance ('as stated on their class syllabus and/or course content'). P04 chosen because the rule is set per instructor.
units.anchor: AI policy as stated on their class syllabus and/or course content
units.policy: AI use is governed by the instructor's AI policy as stated in the class syllabus and/or course content (e.g. canvas page, assignment instructions, examination instructions, assessment instructions).

documents.title: AR 3775 Acceptable Use of Generative AI (draft as of 04/23/2026)
documents.summary: A draft acceptable-use regulation for employees and other authorized District users, covering governance, approved tools, data privacy, disclosure, bias, training and enforcement. It excludes students and refers their use to academic integrity rules. It is not confirmed as adopted.
documents.stance_why: The regulation governs employees and authorized users and says 'Student use of AI tools is governed by applicable Board Policies and Administrative Regulations related to academic integrity', so it sets no stance on student AI use and defers elsewhere.

units.why: The purpose statement says AI 'has the potential to enhance instructional quality, operational efficiency, innovation, and decision-making when used responsibly', naming benefits. P87 fits as it states benefits without a rule.
units.anchor: has the potential to enhance instructional quality, operational efficiency, innovation, and decision-making

units.why: The regulation 'establishes a governance and acceptable use framework' stating purpose and principles ('ethical, lawful, secure, and transparent use'). P56 fits as an institution-level framework preamble.
units.anchor: establishes a governance and acceptable use framework for the ethical, lawful, secure, and transparent use

units.why: The scope sentence says the regulation applies to employees, contractors and other users of District resources, which sets who is bound; P56 (scope) fits better than P61 because it is not a definition of AI.
units.anchor: applies to all District employees, contractors, consultants, volunteers, and other individuals

units.why: The text says 'Student use of AI tools is governed by applicable Board Policies and Administrative Regulations related to academic integrity', carving students out and deferring to integrity rules. P77 fits since it points to existing policy; P04 does not since no instructor discretion is stated.
units.anchor: Student use of AI tools is governed by applicable Board Policies and Administrative Regulations

units.why: The definitions define AI as 'Computer systems designed to perform tasks that typically require human intelligence', setting the scope; P61 fits exactly.
units.anchor: Computer systems designed to perform tasks that typically require human intelligence

units.why: GenAI is defined as 'A subset of AI that generates new content such as text, images, audio, video, or code', a definition of scope (P61).
units.anchor: generates new content such as text, images, audio, video, or code

units.why: The definition of 'AI Tool' as 'Any software, platform, or service that uses AI or GenAI capabilities, including AI Agents' widens scope to embedded tools and agents; P61 chosen as a definition, with a fit note because it also reaches agents (P07).
units.anchor: Any software, platform, or service that uses AI or GenAI capabilities, including AI Agents
units.fit_note: Also brings AI agents and embedded AI-enabled software within scope, which P07 concerns for coding tools.

units.why: 'Sensitive Data' is defined to include 'student education records, personally identifiable information' etc., setting what privacy rules protect; a definition so P61 (scope definitions) fits.
units.anchor: Information protected by law or District policy, including but not limited to student education records
units.frag_start: Sensitive Data: Information protected by law
units.fit_note: Defines sensitive data rather than AI itself; it sets the scope of the data-protection rules.

units.why: 'The Vice President responsible for Information Technology, or designee, shall serve as the executive authority for AI governance' names who owns the policy; P80 fits.
units.anchor: shall serve as the executive authority for AI governance and oversight
units.frag_start: The Vice President responsible for Information

units.why: The District 'may establish an AI governance body or advisory group' with listed membership; naming a body that implements and monitors the policy fits P80.
units.anchor: The District may establish an AI governance body or advisory group

units.why: The governance body may 'Review and recommend approved AI tools' and 'Establish standards, guidelines, and risk assessments', i.e. institutional review of tools; P65 fits (P80 names the body, this is its tool-review function).
units.anchor: Review and recommend approved AI tools

units.why: The body may 'Recommend updates based on legal, technological, and regulatory developments', a commitment to revise the policy over time; P54 fits.
units.anchor: Recommend updates based on legal, technological, and regulatory developments

units.why: 'Only AI tools reviewed and approved through District governance processes may be used for District business where District data or systems are involved' restricts use to approved tools; P92 fits since it is institution-wide approved-tool use, and P65 (the review process) is covered by another unit.
units.anchor: Only AI tools reviewed and approved through District governance processes may be used

units.why: Acceptable use allows 'approved AI tools to support District-related activities' provided they advance objectives and comply with law; it permits employee use under conditions. P59 fits as staff use for work, with a fit note since it also covers administrative work.
units.anchor: Authorized users may use approved AI tools to support District-related activities
units.fit_note: Covers all authorized users and administrative and operational activities, not only teaching work.

units.why: The condition that use 'Complies with applicable laws, regulations, Board Policies, and Administrative Regulations' requires compliance with existing law and policy (P77).
units.anchor: Complies with applicable laws, regulations, Board Policies, and Administrative Regulations

units.why: The condition that use 'Preserves human oversight and accountability' and 'Does not replace professional judgment' keeps humans responsible; P73 fits better than P46 because it is about decisions generally, not grading.
units.anchor: Does not replace professional judgment or decision-making where human review is required

units.why: Prohibited use bans 'Inputting, uploading, or processing sensitive or confidential District data into unapproved AI tools', a data-protection rule; P50 fits (P49 is students and course materials).
units.anchor: Inputting, uploading, or processing sensitive or confidential District data into unapproved AI tools

units.why: The prohibition on using AI 'to make final decisions related to employment actions, student evaluation, discipline, or legal determinations without required human review' keeps humans responsible for decisions about people (P73).
units.anchor: Using AI tools to make final decisions related to employment actions, student evaluation, discipline
units.frag_start: Using AI tools to make final

units.why: Banning 'Misrepresenting AI-generated content as solely human-created where disclosure is required' makes nondisclosure where required a violation; P28 fits.
units.anchor: Misrepresenting AI-generated content as solely human-created where disclosure is required

units.why: The ban on AI 'for unlawful, unethical, discriminatory, or harassing purposes' is a general conduct rule against malicious use (P74).
units.anchor: Using AI tools for unlawful, unethical, discriminatory, or harassing purposes

units.why: 'Circumventing District security, privacy, or governance controls' is prohibited; it is a security-breach conduct rule, fitting P74 only partly.
units.anchor: Circumventing District security, privacy, or governance controls
units.fit_note: Concerns circumventing controls of the District rather than deception or malware specifically.

units.why: 'Users shall not input sensitive or confidential District data into AI systems unless explicitly authorized and compliant with FERPA, HIPAA...' is a data-protection rule with legal compliance; P50 chosen as the data rule, not P77.
units.anchor: Users shall not input sensitive or confidential District data into AI systems unless explicitly authorized

units.why: 'AI tools must meet District information security standards, including data encryption, access controls, vendor risk assessments' sets review and security requirements for tools (P65).
units.anchor: AI tools must meet District information security standards, including data encryption, access controls

units.why: 'AI vendors must not retain, reuse, or train models on District data unless expressly authorized' limits data sharing with AI providers; P65 as broadened covers it.
units.anchor: AI vendors must not retain, reuse, or train models on District data

units.why: 'Users must clearly disclose when AI tools are used to generate content that materially informs decisions, communications, or instructional materials' requires disclosure of AI use by employees. P48 would cover only course materials; P24 fits the general disclosure duty.
units.anchor: Users must clearly disclose when AI tools are used to generate content
units.fit_note: Applies to employees and covers decisions and communications as well as instructional materials, not student submissions.

units.why: 'The District shall promote transparency regarding institutional uses of AI that impact students, employees, or the public' commits to telling people about institutional AI use (P103).
units.anchor: promote transparency regarding institutional uses of AI that impact students
units.fit_note: Commits to transparency about institutional uses in general, not specifically to telling a person they are dealing with an AI system.

units.why: Under the Bias heading, 'Users must be aware that AI systems may reflect or amplify bias' and must 'identify, mitigate, and document potential bias', naming bias concerns; P53 fits.
units.anchor: AI systems may reflect or amplify bias

units.why: 'AI-generated outputs must be reviewed by humans prior to use in decision-making, instructional, or operational contexts' requires verification of AI output; P31 fits.
units.anchor: AI-generated outputs must be reviewed by humans prior to use

units.why: The District 'endorses ethical AI principles that emphasize human accountability, fairness, transparency, and responsible innovation, with due consideration for environmental impacts', naming ethical and environmental concerns; P53 fits.
units.anchor: with due consideration for environmental impacts
units.frag_start: The District endorses ethical AI principles
units.fit_note: Also states positive principles (accountability, fairness, transparency), not only concerns.

units.why: 'The District shall promote AI literacy by providing guidance, training, and resources to employees' commits to training for staff; P70 fits.
units.anchor: The District shall promote AI literacy by providing guidance, training, and resources to employees

units.why: 'Completion of training may be required prior to the use of certain AI tools' makes training a possible precondition; P70 covers mandated training.
units.anchor: Completion of training may be required prior to the use of certain AI tools

units.why: 'Violation of this regulation may result in suspension or revocation of access to AI tools, disciplinary action, and/or legal consequences' states penalties; P37 fits.
units.anchor: may result in suspension or revocation of access to AI tools, disciplinary action

notes: AR 5500.1 is a marked-up draft with typos; its AI sentence appears twice and is coded once per rule. AR 3775 is a draft; adoption unconfirmed. Topic codes follow tools/AGENT_BRIEF.md.
